summary: Phase 2.5 — the diary wedge — shipped end-to-end. Library got the 'journal' AttestationKind (7 kinds now), the journalAttestation builder, the envelope-whitelist update, and the per-kind test. Wallet got a new journal feature (composer with text + subject picker + category picker + photo upload, card with live anchor-status badge, tabs by category, detail view with photo + signers + anchor block height + save-to-files download) and a new anchoring feature (OpenTimestamps provider singleton consuming tapit-attest's already-fetch-based OpenTimestampsProvider, IDB-backed anchor queue keyed by attestation digest, background worker that scans on app mount + polls every 5 minutes while open + pauses on offline + resumes on online via navigator events, useAnchorStatus + useAnchorWorker hooks). Storage extended with mediaStore for SHA-256-keyed encrypted photo bytes. WalletProvider exposes passphrase + anchorWorker through context; passphrase cleared on sign-out. HomeScreen hosts JournalTabs above a floating + New entry button that opens the composer inline. The grandchild scenario is now reachable end-to-end — operator can sign 'Grandson Tom Jr born on date at hospital' with a photo and watch it cycle queued → pending → confirmed-at-Bitcoin-block.

why.text: Operator greenlit Phase 2.5 with the OTS port pulled forward and explicitly named the time-delay lifecycle as needing helpers — answered with the anchor queue + background worker pattern. The pre-cut investigation found that tapit-attest's OpenTimestampsProvider was already dependency-free (the brief's port-from-AppCommander recommendation predated the library's current state), which let me focus the session on lifecycle plumbing rather than re-implementing the protocol. User-sovereign default per operator's directive: photos stay in encrypted IndexedDB with save-to-files download; no Supabase Storage bucket; paid hosted-storage tier deferred entirely.

files_changed: 27 files: 4 library files modified, 13 new wallet files across 2 new features (journal, anchoring) + media store, plus updates to WalletProvider, HomeScreen, App, registry, and the storage manifest.
outcome.tests_passing: root 16/16 (manifest-registry correctly picked up the 2 new slugs). tapit-attest 74/74 active, 4 skipped — the journal-kind round-trip test passes.
outcome.notes: Commit f299c7d on branch + main (fast-forward). Bundle posture: login surface unchanged ~110KB gzipped; new lazy chunks JournalDetail 1.61KB gz, anchorQueue 0.77KB gz, useAnchorStatus 2.83KB gz; HomeScreen grew to 3.69KB gz; WalletProvider 3.54KB gz; attest chunk grew to 25.17KB gz to carry the new journal builder export. NOT VERIFIED in a browser — sandbox has no browser. Operator should walk: sign-in → home → '+ New entry' → fill text + subject ('Someone else' → label) + category + photo → 'Sign this entry' → home shows the new card with 'Anchor queued' → wait/refresh → 'Anchored — waiting on Bitcoin confirmation' → eventually 'Confirmed at Bitcoin block NNN'.

uncertainty: End-to-end against a real OpenTimestamps calendar has not been verified — the provider is the existing tapit-attest implementation which has unit-level coverage against fake transports but the live-network round-trip is operator-side. Anchor worker behavior under flaky-network / app-backgrounding scenarios is also browser-runtime-dependent. If anything stalls, the failure modes are: (1) STAMP fails → row stays in failed state, retried every 5 min; (2) UPGRADE returns pending forever → row stays pending; (3) status badge stuck → useAnchorStatus reactivity issue. Each is debuggable.
next: Operator browser-verifies Phase 2.5 against real Supabase + real OTS calendar. If clean, Phase 2.6 (multi-witness co-signing via in-person QR exchange + custody-handoff mechanism for the grandchild scenario) is the next cutting session. If anything stalls, the next session diagnoses and fixes before proceeding. Phase 2.7 (documents) reuses the photo path. Then Phase 3 (Nostr NIP-46) and Phase 5 (Mycelium peer + Shamir recovery) per the brief's mapping.
